question: What does pgrepair do to 3,932 wrong type labels when its Step 2 (--label-repair) is enabled, as its own documentation prescribes for label errors?
graph: runs/seven/graph.json — the frozen EUR-Lex truth with the seven-damages injection, journal runs/seven/journal.json
the law: L6 — an act's type label says what its CELEX says (workloads/eurlex-labels.toml), then the edge laws (workloads/eurlex-laws.toml)
command: runs/seven/label-repair.sh 3 — pg-repair-run --commit repair --label-repair -a SciPyWeightedILP on the label law (committed for real, no --mark), then --commit repair --mark on the edge laws; read with corrige.neo4j_graph; judged by runs/seven/judge_label_repair.py against the truth and the journal

measured.label pass, each run: found a solution with weight 3930 · Repairing by deleting 0 edge(s), 0 node(s), 3930 labels
measured.edge pass, each run: Repairing by deleting 687 edge(s), 0 node(s), 0 labels

against the earlier figure.label-repair-two-ways-2026-09-13 and the: 3,930 nodes deleted, 11,200 true facts lost — those runs did not pass --label-repair, so Step 2 was off and pgrepair could only delete nodes (its §4.3: nodes are deleted only for isolated-node errors; Step 2 exists to remove labels instead).
against the earlier figure.what it means: The 11,200 was a configuration of ours, not a behaviour of the tool. With Step 2 on, the collateral is zero.

reading: With Step 2, pgrepair removes every wrong type label and destroys nothing: 0 nodes, 0 true facts, on three identical runs (the label pass deletes 0 edges; the edge pass that follows deletes 687, as before).

It does not write the right label. Deleting the wrong :Decision leaves the node without a type label; the type survives only in the celex_type property — the second witness. The Cypher repair of label-repair-two-ways writes it back: 3,930 set right. The contrast is delete-the-false versus write-the-true, which is exactly PVLDB 2026 §7 (combine deletion with insertion techniques).

By pgrepair's own quality measure — the number of deletions — the two repairs count the same, 3,930. Only an external ground truth separates 11,200 true facts lost from zero. That is the whole reason the bench exists.

This supersedes the cause given in label-repair-retracted-2026-09-13: the 13:16:52 run was not only three minutes ahead of the loader; it was the one run with the flag. The retraction's conclusion stands — nothing better was found by accident — its cause was incomplete.
what this does not say: Not run on the night injection (seven damages incl. ANACHRONISM; runs/night/journal.json, embedded sha256 df640987dd868977…, on disk and replayable). The 12,591 of reachability-by-damage-2026-09-10 is that injection, Step 2 off; it is retired from the memos in favour of the corrected configuration measured here, not because it cannot be replayed.
Whether Step 2 leaves the same 3,930 nodes untyped on the night injection is not measured.
journal_sha256: ced2627844564cfb… (the journal's own embedded sha256; the raw file hashes to 3c92f666…)

counted afterwards, not only read from t.nodes without a type label: 68,525 in runs/seven/graph.json, 72,455 in each of the three candidates — 3,930 more, identical on the three runs. Step 2 erased the wrong label and wrote none.
counted afterwards, not only read from t.why 3,930 labels for 3,932 injected: 3,932 WRONG_LABEL events on 3,932 distinct nodes. Five of those nodes were absorbed by a MERGE of the same injection and are no longer in the graph; three split twins (…#split) violate L6 too and are erased as well. 3,932 − 5 + 3 = 3,930. The judge reports all 3,932 violations gone.
counted afterwards, not only read from t.this corrects label-repair-two-ways-2026: its sentence 'two of the injected labels are invisible to the CELEX check, and they are the same two pgrepair does not reach either' is withdrawn: no such pair exists on this graph; the gap is the five merged nodes and the three twins.
